actions.name: get_capabilities
actions.title: List capabilities
actions.description: Lists every registered action grouped by group, with the procedures and the contract hash. Call this first when you have not yet seen this product's procedures. Example: get_capabilities({}).

actions.name: list_week_events
actions.title: List week events
actions.description: Lists door events and the visits built from them for one day or the whole record, oldest first. Use it to read a day before deciding what to open; it never changes anything, and all times are local to the household. A question from the person is answered from reads like this one: look the record up yourself instead of asking which day or door they mean (the household has one front door and one hall camera), and change nothing unless they ask you to. Days are numbered from Monday 5 Oct = 0, so the review week runs Monday 12 Oct = 7, Tuesday 13 Oct = 8, up to Sunday 18 Oct = 13. Example: list_week_events({"day": 8, "limit": 20}).

day.description: Absolute day index: 0 = Mon 5 Oct, 7 = Mon 12 Oct, 13 = Sun 18 Oct.

deviceId.description: Device id such as dev-door, or its name such as Front door.

type.description: Event type to keep; omit for all types.

actions.name: get_incident
actions.title: Get incident
actions.description: Returns one incident with its notes and attached evidence (labels only, not image data). Use it before changing an incident's status; incident ids come from list_week_events, compare_to_baseline or check_week_model, never from the person. Example: get_incident({"incidentId": "inc-1"}).

actions.name: get_rhythm_baseline
actions.title: Get rhythm baseline
actions.description: Returns the household's usual rhythm from the baseline week: the longest-stay figure (90th percentile, in minutes), the median stay, the number of visits it is based on, the busiest hours and the daily routines. Call it once before comparing days. Example: get_rhythm_baseline({}).

actions.name: list_devices
actions.title: List devices
actions.description: Lists the household's Ring devices with their components and whether each can play audio, show live video or take a snapshot. Use it to find device ids and names, to check a capability before proposing an action that needs it, and to answer which cameras are online; call it yourself instead of asking the person. Example: list_devices({}).

actions.name: get_device_status
actions.title: Get device status
actions.description: Reads a device's current status from Ring: online or offline, power source and battery level. Use it when a device looks silent in the record. Example: get_device_status({"deviceId": "dev-elite"}).

actions.name: get_device_capabilities
actions.title: Get device capabilities
actions.description: Reads what a device, or one of its components, can do: motion detection, live video, snapshot and chime audio. Use it before relying on a capability. Example: get_device_capabilities({"deviceId": "dev-elite", "componentId": 1}).

componentId.description: Camera component, 0 or 1 on the hall camera.

actions.name: ingest_ring_events
actions.title: Ingest ring events
actions.description: Brings new events into the record, either the webhooks waiting in the inbox or a device's event history. Events are added by id only, so the same moment seen on both channels stays as two events until merge_duplicate_events folds them. Example: ingest_ring_events({"source": "history", "deviceId": "dev-door"}).

deviceId.description: Device id or name; required when source is history.

sinceMs.description: Only events at or after this UTC millisecond time; default the start of the record.

actions.name: merge_duplicate_events
actions.title: Merge duplicate events
actions.description: Folds events that are the same moment seen twice into the earliest one. Use it on the ids named by a duplicate issue from check_week_model, and only on ids that belong to one duplicate group. There is one group per issue and a week can hold dozens, so send the calls for several groups together in the same step instead of one at a time. Example: merge_duplicate_events({"eventIds": ["evt:req-a", "hist:b"]}).

eventIds.description: Ids of events that are the same moment seen twice.

actions.name: reconcile_webhook_gap
actions.title: Reconcile webhook gap
actions.description: Fills the gap left when a device's webhooks went quiet by reading its event history from the last webhook onward, skipping events already in the record. Use it for each device before comparing days; with overlapMinutes 0 nothing already known is read again. Example: reconcile_webhook_gap({"deviceId": "dev-elite", "overlapMinutes": 0}).

overlapMinutes.description: Minutes before the last webhook to start reading, default 10.

actions.name: open_incident
actions.title: Open incident
actions.description: Opens an incident for something that stood out and, by default, attaches a snapshot from the device as evidence. Use the kind, title, eventIds, startMs, endMs, routineId and dayIndex exactly as a finding, an issue fix or a visit from list_week_events gives them. Open an incident only when the person asks you to note, mark or flag a moment, never to answer a question. Example: open_incident({"kind": "quiet_hours_activity", "title": "Door activity at 02:14 during quiet hours", "eventIds": ["evt:req-9"], "startMs": 1791000000000, "endMs": 1791001000000, "dayIndex": 8}).

eventIds.description: Event ids behind the incident; empty only for missed_routine.

routineId.description: Routine id for a missed routine.

startMs.description: Start of the incident in UTC milliseconds.

endMs.description: End of the incident in UTC milliseconds.

withSnapshot.description: Attach a snapshot from the device as evidence, default true.

actions.name: set_incident_status
actions.title: Set incident status
actions.description: Moves an incident to a new status and, when given, stores the explanation the family will read. Use explained once a note has been written, resolved when the family member has dealt with it, and dismissed when it was not a concern. Use it only when the person asks you to mark or close a moment. To mark a visit they name (for example the Tuesday evening visit): find it with list_week_events for that day, call open_incident for it, then call this with the new incident's id and the person's own words as the summary; do all of that yourself without asking them for an id, a time or a name. Example: set_incident_status({"incidentId": "inc-1", "status": "explained", "summary": "A visit at 02:14 lasted 22 min."}).

summary.description: Plain-language explanation shown to the family.

actions.name: check_week_model
actions.title: Check week model
actions.description: Runs every rule over the record and returns the issues with a suggested fix for each, plus the error and warning counts. Call it after reading and recording, and again after every repair until it reports zero errors. Example: check_week_model({}).

actions.name: compare_to_baseline
actions.title: Compare to baseline
actions.description: Compares one day with the household's baseline and returns the visit count, the longest stay against the usual figure, quiet-hours visits, routines kept and missed, and a list of findings that could become incidents. Use the findings' fields as they are when opening an incident. Findings are candidates only: open an incident for the single moment the person asked about, never one for every finding. Example: compare_to_baseline({"day": 8}).

day.description: Absolute day index; review days are 7 to 13.

actions.name: focus_day
actions.title: Focus day
actions.description: Moves the view to one day so the person watching sees what you are reading. It changes nothing in the record. Use it whenever the person says show me, or asks what happened on a day: showing a day means calling this, and describing it in words does not show it. Days are numbered from Monday 5 Oct = 0, so the review week runs Monday 12 Oct = 7, Tuesday 13 Oct = 8, up to Sunday 18 Oct = 13. Example: focus_day({"day": 8}).

day.description: Day to show, or null to show the whole week.

actions.name: focus_incident
actions.title: Focus incident
actions.description: Selects an incident in the view, moves to its day and frames it in the 3D scene. Use it when you start working on an incident. Example: focus_incident({"incidentId": "inc-1"}).

actions.name: set_camera_shot
actions.title: Set camera shot
actions.description: Chooses the camera shot of the 3D doorway view: the whole week, a walk along a visitor's path, or a close frame on one incident. It changes only the view. Example: set_camera_shot({"shot": "overview"}).

actions.name: add_incident_note
actions.title: Add incident note
actions.description: Adds a short note to an incident so the family can see what you saw. Write one plain sentence using only facts from function results. Example: add_incident_note({"incidentId": "inc-1", "text": "The front door saw activity at 02:14, inside quiet hours."}).

text.description: One plain sentence about what was seen.

actions.name: propose_family_nudge
actions.title: Propose family nudge
actions.description: Prepares one gentle message for the family member to send, shown as a decision card. It is only a proposal: the family member approves or rejects it, and it needs the Family message consent to be on. Example: propose_family_nudge({"incidentId": "inc-1", "text": "Maybe a quick call this evening?"}).

text.description: One short, kind message for the family member to approve.

actions.name: play_chime_announcement
actions.title: Play chime announcement
actions.description: Plays a short chime on the front-door device so someone at home hears a gentle sound. It reaches a person, so it needs the Chime announcement consent and the family member's approval each time, and it works only on a device that can play audio. Example: play_chime_announcement({"deviceId": "dev-door", "audioRef": "gentle_hello"}).

deviceId.description: Device id or name; must support chime audio.

actions.name: export_weekly_brief
actions.title: Export weekly brief
actions.description: Builds the weekly brief from the record and shares it with the family. It leaves the product, so it needs the Weekly brief consent and the family member's approval each time. Example: export_weekly_brief({"includeNotes": true}).

includeNotes.description: Include the incident notes in the brief.

procedures.name: review_week
steps: For each device returned by list_devices, call reconcile_webhook_gap with overlapMinutes 0. A device whose webhooks went quiet has its missing events filled in from the event history.
For each focus day in the plan (all of days 7 to 13 when none are given), call compare_to_baseline with that day. Several calls may go out in the same turn.

For each finding that is a real change from the household's rhythm (a visit during quiet hours, a stay well above the usual, a device offline for over 30 minutes, a routine that did not happen), call open_incident with the finding's kind, title, eventIds, startMs, endMs, routineId and dayIndex exactly as returned, then call add_incident_note with one plain sentence about what you saw.
Call check_week_model and read its issues.
Reply in two or three sentences: what you opened, and the counts check_week_model returned.

procedures.name: repair_errors
steps: For each issue with severity error, call the action named in the issue's fix with the arguments given. Do not change the arguments.
Call check_week_model again. Repeat until it reports zero errors or your turns run out.
Reply in two sentences: what you changed and the final counts.

procedures.name: prepare_family_update
steps: Call propose_family_nudge once, for the most important open incident, with one short kind sentence. The family member decides on it.
Call export_weekly_brief once. It waits for the family member's approval.
If a chime on the front door would reassure and list_devices shows the device can play audio, call play_chime_announcement once with audioRef "gentle_hello".
When any call is refused or declined, do not retry it. Reply in two sentences: what was done, and what the family member could switch on.
